solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: American buffoon returned, remote in manner

indicators.note: returned means the word for buffoon is sent back, read right to left

explanation.surface: An American clown has come home, and is now cool and standoffish.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof keeps a distance from others, cool and reserved in their bearing.

clue.text: Primate by crown

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as 'by' in measurements like 3 x 4

explanation.surface: A monkey standing beside a crown.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex of something is its top or summit, as a crown is the top of the head.

clue.text: Haughty and dogmatic concerning deportment

parts.note: over can mean concerning, as in a row over money
bearing means deportment, how one carries oneself

explanation.surface: A stiff, arrogant attitude about how one should carry oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: An overbearing person is domineering and arrogant, imposing their views on others.

clue.text: Best penalties, ultimate in sport

indicators.note: ultimate in means the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: The best penalties of all, the last word in sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The finest is the highest in quality, the very best available.

clue.text: Easy to name donkey

explanation.surface: A donkey that is easy to give a name to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Donkey' is the informal sense: a foolish, slow-witted person.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a donkey is calling them a fool, which is exactly what a simpleton is.

clue.text: Shop stocks nothing but drink in here?

indicators.note: stocks means holds within, so the shop word contains the letter for nothing

parts.note: a salon is a shop, such as a hairdresser's
bar means but or except, as in all bar one

explanation.surface: A shop that stocks nothing except drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A saloon bar is the more comfortable lounge room of a British pub; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a room in a pub where people sit and have a pint.

clue.text: Someone like Scrooge can cause endless grief

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

explanation.surface: A Scrooge figure can bring endless sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's Ebenezer Scrooge is the classic hoarder of money who hates spending it.

clue.text: A golf rep arranged game

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A golf representative has organised a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapfrog is a playground pastime where children vault over each other's bent backs.

clue.text: Briefly carry toddler

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: Carrying a toddler for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small child, someone just learning to walk.

clue.text: Silly-billy's wages short after note found on deck

indicators.note: after means the shortened wages word follows the note
found on means placed above, in a down clue, the word for deck
short means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the poop is the raised deck at a ship's stern

explanation.surface: A fool, his pay docked, turns up on the ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A nincompoop is a foolish, stupid person, the same as a silly-billy.

clue.text: European seabird by a lake unaffected by time

parts.note: L is a standard abbreviation for lake, as on maps

explanation.surface: A European seabird beside a lake that seems untouched by the passing years.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting has no beginning or end, so the years never change it.

clue.text: Disciplined person's skill during bridge

indicators.note: during means one word sits within the time, and so the letters, of another

parts.note: a span is a bridge, or the stretch it crosses
art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A disciplined player shows real skill at the bridge table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' looks like the card game but is the structure. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens of ancient Sparta were famed for austere self-control, so the name now means a strict, hardy person.

clue.text: Singer and graduates likewise, in favour of enjoyable party

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates
so means likewise, as in 'so do I'

explanation.surface: A singer and some graduates, all keen on a good party.
explanation.definitionFit: A basso profundo is a bass singer with an exceptionally deep voice range.

clue.text: Foreign name sounds about right for this popular aria

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumbled letters surround the letter for right
foreign means strange or unfamiliar, so the letters of name sounds are jumbled

explanation.surface: A foreign title sounds about right for this famous aria.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of NAME SOUNDS gives NESSUNDOMA, and 'about' wraps it around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessun Dorma is the tenor showpiece from Puccini's Turandot, made a hit by Pavarotti at the 1990 World Cup.

clue.text: Misleading clue embarrassed Holmes, initially slipping up

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is taken

parts.note: erring means making a mistake, slipping up

explanation.surface: A false lead leaves Sherlock Holmes blushing at his own mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is a distraction that diverts attention from the truth, a false trail.

clue.text: Produced round cheese

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the word for produced is read backwards

explanation.surface: A cheese has been made in a round shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a description of the cheese, but it signals turning the word around.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a Dutch cheese, typically sold in a red-waxed ball.

clue.text: Toast made by Shakespearean character having drink

parts.note: Bottom is the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A toast proposed by a Shakespeare character over a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a cheerful drinking salute, said as glasses are raised and emptied.

clue.text: Cheap flat

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes both poor style and food or drink with no real flavour.

clue.text: Messaging symbol illustrates feeling when nursing cold

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the feeling word contains the letter for cold

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A text symbol shows how you feel when you are nursing a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: An emoticon is a small face built from keyboard characters, used in texts to show mood.

clue.text: Engulfing rear of rectory, bad weather spoils prayers

indicators.note: engulfing means the weather words swallow the letter, holding it inside
rear of means the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: Storms ruin the vicarage, and the prayers go up.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hail Mary is a Catholic devotion to the Virgin, a prayer recited often in a rosary.

clue.text: Awfully loud children's game

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of loud are jumbled

explanation.surface: A noisy board game for kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a simple dice-and-counters board game played by youngsters.

clue.text: Fellow holding very soft pelt

indicators.note: holding means the word for fellow contains the other letters

parts.note: a peer is a fellow or equal
PP is pianissimo, the musical mark for very soft

explanation.surface: A man clutching a very soft animal skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' looks like a noun, an animal skin, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pepper someone is to bombard them with many small missiles, as with shot or questions.

clue.text: Bishop always tracking rook in accurate finish

indicators.note: tracking means following behind, so the word for always comes after the rook

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess bishop always chasing a rook towards a precise endgame.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess pieces mislead: 'Bishop' is the churchman, and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Right Reverend is the formal style of address for an Anglican bishop.

clue.text: Scoffed at during poetic evening

indicators.note: during means inside, so the word at goes within the poetic word

parts.note: e'en is a poetic contraction of evening

explanation.surface: Someone was mocked at a poetry evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' suggests jeering, but here it means gobbled.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is to eat it greedily, so scoffed food has been consumed.

clue.text: Ancient city, partially destroyed

indicators.note: partially means only part of the next word is used, its letters lying within it

explanation.surface: An old city, partly in ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy was the city besieged by the Greeks in Homer's Iliad, later sacked and burned.

clue.text: I caught it sitting next to poorly criminal

indicators.note: sitting next to means the other pieces are placed beside the word for poorly

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to catching a bug while sitting by a sick criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit means forbidden by law, so an illicit act is a criminal one.

clue.text: Not quite striking rising tennis shot

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, means the letters are read from bottom to top
not quite means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: striking means bold, as in a bold colour

explanation.surface: A rising shot in tennis that does not quite hit cleanly.
explanation.definitionFit: A lob is a high, looping stroke hit over an opponent at the net.

clue.text: Perhaps Hadrian's mood heading off with enlisted men

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed from the word for mood

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, enlisted soldiers

explanation.surface: Hadrian, in a mood, marches off with his soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks Hadrian as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hadrian was a Roman ruler who reigned from AD 117, famous for his wall in northern Britain.

clue.text: Flip one's lid and crack crackers

parts.note: a crack is an attempt, a go
crackers means crazy, as does bananas

explanation.surface: Losing one's temper and cracking up completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for losing control and becoming wild with anger or excitement.

clue.text: Look at first of Yorkshires made beforehand

parts.note: to read something is to look at it

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Checking whether the Yorkshire puddings were made in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshires are Yorkshire puddings, baked batter cakes served with roast beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ready has been prepared in advance, as in ready meals.
